title: The image of an idempotent endomorphism of a finite free module is finite projective and commutes with base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ and $p:R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus n}$ an $R$-linear map with $p\circ p=p$, with matrix $X\in M_n(R)$ in the standard basis. (i) $R^{\oplus n}=\operatorname{Im}(p)\oplus\operatorname{Im}(1-p)$ (internal direct sum, with $\operatorname{Im}(1-p)=\ker p$), so $\operatorname{Im}(p)$ is a finite projective $R$-module (a direct summand of a finite free module). (ii) Let $\rho:R\to S$ be a ring map and $p_S:S^{\oplus n}\to S^{\oplus n}$ the $S$-linear map with matrix $\rho(X)$ (entrywise); then $p_S\circ p_S=p_S$, and the $S$-linear map $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS\to S^{\oplus n}$, $v\otimes s\mapsto s\cdot\rho(v)$ ($\rho$ applied to coordinates), is injective with image $\operatorname{Im}(p_S)$; hence $\operatorname{Im}(p)\otimes_RS\cong\operatorname{Im}(p_S)$ as $S$-modules.

proof.text: Use LinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.ker_eq_range_one_sub and isCompl to identify Im(1-p) with ker(p) and prove complementarity. Module.Finite.range gives finiteness. The restriction of p to its range is a retraction of the subtype inclusion, so Module.Projective.of_split gives projectivity from the finite free ambient module.

proof.text: Let E be TensorProduct.piScalarRight, the canonical S-linear equivalence S tensor_R R^n to S^n. Base-change the inclusion i of range(p) and the retraction r induced by p. The identity r composed with i = id holds on pure tensors. Set f = E composed with i and g = r composed with E inverse; then g composed with f = id. On pure tensors f(s tensor x) has coordinates s rho(x_j), by the tensor base-change formulas [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property].

proof.text: On pure tensors compute E(i(r(s tensor x))) using RingHom.map_mulVec and LinearMap.toMatrix'_mulVec; it agrees with p_S(E(s tensor x)). Therefore f composed with g = p_S. The two split-map identities imply p_S squared = p_S, f is injective, and range(f)=range(p_S). LinearEquiv.ofInjective followed by LinearEquiv.ofEq yields the required canonical range equivalence and subtype compatibility.

lean.statement: theorem idempotent_image_baseChange {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (p : Module.End R (Fin n → R)) (hp : IsIdempotentElem p) {S : Type v} [CommRing S] (ρ : R →+* S) : letI : Algebra R S := ρ.toAlgebra let pS : Module.End S (Fin n → S) := Matrix.toLin' ((LinearMap.toMatrix' p).map ρ) IsCompl p.range (1 - p).range ∧ (1 - p).range = p.ker ∧ Module.Finite R p.range ∧ Module.Projective R p.range ∧ IsIdempotentElem pS ∧ ∃ f : S ⊗[R] p.range →ₗ[S] (Fin n → S), (∀ (s : S) (x : p.range), f (s ⊗ₜ[R] x) = fun i ↦ s * ρ (x.val i)) ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ f.range = pS.range ∧ ∃ e : S ⊗[R] p.range ≃ₗ[S] pS.range, pS.range.subtype.comp e.toLinearMap = f
